evals.prompt: /cheatsheet-scribe Topic: Ollama CLI. Audience: developers new to local LLMs. My notes: install on Linux with `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`, run a model with `ollama run llama3.2`, list local models with `ollama list`, remove one with `ollama rm <model>`. Homepage https://ollama.com, repo https://github.com/ollama/ollama.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks for an existing ollama cheatsheet, drafts from the notes only, writes src/content/cheatsheets/<slug>/<slug>.md, runs the lint, asks 2-4 specific review questions, and after approval prints Result/Evidence/Uncertainty/Decision plus a commit message without committing.
expectations: Checks src/content/cheatsheets/<slug>/ for an existing cheatsheet before writing any file
Uses only the commands and URLs given in the notes; anything else is marked unverified
Runs `pnpm cheatsheet:lint src/content/cheatsheets/<slug>/<slug>.md --no-links` and reports its exit code
Asks 2-4 content-specific review questions and waits for answers before the final response
Does not stage, commit, or push
Final response opens with complete/partial/blocked and the file path
Final response labels unverified items and checks not run separately from verified results
Each material claim in the final response points to a note, provided URL, lint result, or contributor answer
Final response states 'No approval needed' and names the next action (stage, commit, open the PR)

evals.prompt:
Write a cheatsheet about the MCP filesystem server for Claude Code users. Here is the README excerpt I copied:

Run with npx: `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /Users/username/Desktop /path/to/other/allowed/dir`

Add this to your claude_desktop_config.json:
{"mcpServers": {"filesystem": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/Users/username/Desktop", "/path/to/other/allowed/dir"]}}}
evals.expected_output: The agent sets category `mcp`, drafts from the pasted excerpt, asks for any missing fact instead of guessing, lints the file, and asks specific review questions.
expectations: Sets frontmatter category to `mcp`
Asks for missing inputs (such as the homepage URL) in a single message instead of inventing them
Places every command in its own fenced block with a language tag and `<UPPER_SNAKE>` placeholders
Prints a Step Completion Report after the lint step
Final response opens with complete/partial/blocked and the file path
Final response states 'No approval needed' and names the contributor's next action

evals.prompt: create cheatsheet: a comparison of git worktrees vs separate clones for running parallel coding agents. My notes: `git worktree add ../wt-feature -b feature`, `git worktree list`, `git worktree remove ../wt-feature`; clones are simpler but duplicate the object store.
evals.expected_output: The agent picks category `comparison`, keeps the locked section order, drafts 3-7 steps with Goal/Time/Level meta and Verify lines, and validates with the lint.
expectations: Sets frontmatter category to `comparison`
Keeps the locked section order from the One-liner through Reference
Writes 3-7 `### Step N — Title` steps, each with a meta line and a Verify line
Groups the verified git commands by goal in the Quick Command Reference
Final response separates verified facts from assumptions

evals.prompt: /cheatsheet-scribe Create a cheatsheet for Hermes Agent.
evals.expected_output: The agent detects src/content/cheatsheets/hermes-agent/, asks for the exact reply 'yes, overwrite', and writes nothing before that reply.
expectations: Detects the existing src/content/cheatsheets/hermes-agent/ directory
Asks the contributor to type 'yes, overwrite' to confirm
Writes no file before receiving that exact reply
If the contributor declines, stops and reports that nothing was written

evals.prompt: Make a cheatsheet for a CLI called fastgrep. I don't have any notes; just include all the commands and flags it probably has.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to guess commands or flags, asks for official docs or notes, and marks any unfilled command as unverified instead of fabricating it.
expectations: Does not invent commands, flags, versions, or URLs
Asks for official docs, a docs link, or notes before filling the Quick Command Reference
Marks unfilled items as unverified and lists them under Uncertainty
Final response reports `partial` or `blocked` rather than `complete` when commands remain unverified

evals.prompt: Change the validator so a step meta line also accepts `**Level:** expert`, and update its unit tests.
evals.expected_output: Task handled as a code change in tools/; the cheatsheet-scribe workflow is not applied.
expectations: The run did not ask for topic, audience, and draft content
The run did not write a file under src/content/cheatsheets/
The run did not print the cheatsheet-scribe review questions or handoff templates
